title: The missing ceiling of the metacyclic bracket
content: The parent chain bounds |Gal(Xⁿ−p/ℚ)| by a two-sided bracket: lower factors n ∣ |Gal| and φ(n) ∣ |Gal| (combining to n·φ(n) ∣ |Gal| when gcd(n,φ(n)) = 1), against the symmetric-group upper bound |Gal| ∣ n!. The squeeze pins the order only when n·φ(n) = n!, i.e. only at n = 2, 3. For n ≥ 4 the factorial bound is loose (n·φ(n) < n!), leaving the order unpinned. This entry supplies the sharp metacyclic ceiling |Gal| ≤ n·φ(n) — unconditionally — via the radical tower ℚ ⊆ ℚ(ζₙ) ⊆ ℚ(ζₙ)(ⁿ√p) = L, the conjectured order n·φ(n) being the order of the holomorph ℤ/n ⋊ (ℤ/n)ˣ.
mathContext: The Galois group of $X^n - p$ embeds in the holomorph $\mathrm{Hol}(\mathbb{Z}/n) = \mathbb{Z}/n \rtimes (\mathbb{Z}/n)^\times$ of order $n\,\varphi(n)$: a root permutation $\beta_i \mapsto \beta_{\sigma(i)}$ is determined by an affine map $i \mapsto ai + b$ with $a \in (\mathbb{Z}/n)^\times$, $b \in \mathbb{Z}/n$. The bracket $n\varphi(n) \mid |\mathrm{Gal}| \mid n!$ collapses to equality only when $n\varphi(n) = n!$, i.e. $n \in \{2,3\}$.

title: The metacyclic ceiling |Gal| ≤ n·φ(n) via the radical tower
content: The ceiling theorem gal_card_le_n_mul_totient (proved in the ancestor InverseGaloisD4OQ02.lean and imported here) rests on two facts, summarized by this docstring bullet. (1) Generation: L = ℚ(ζₙ, α) for a single root α and primitive n-th root ζ — every root β satisfies βⁿ = p = αⁿ, so (β/α)ⁿ = 1 and β = ζⁱ·α, hence the splitting field needs only two generators, not all n roots. (2) Tower degrees: with L = ℚ(ζ)(α), the tower law gives [L:ℚ] = [ℚ(ζ):ℚ]·[L:ℚ(ζ)] = φ(n)·[L:ℚ(ζ)], and [L:ℚ(ζ)] ≤ n because α is a root of the degree-n polynomial Xⁿ − p already over ℚ(ζ). Multiplying: |Gal| = [L:ℚ] ≤ φ(n)·n, strictly sharper than n! for n ≥ 4.
mathContext: The roots of $X^n - p$ are $\{\zeta^i \alpha : 0 \le i < n\}$ with $\alpha = \sqrt[n]{p}$, so $L = \mathbb{Q}(\zeta,\alpha) = \mathbb{Q}(\zeta)(\alpha)$. The tower law $[L:\mathbb{Q}] = [\mathbb{Q}(\zeta):\mathbb{Q}]\cdot[L:\mathbb{Q}(\zeta)]$ has base degree $\deg\Phi_n = \varphi(n)$ (cyclotomic minimal polynomial) and top degree $\deg(\mathrm{minpoly}_{\mathbb{Q}(\zeta)}\alpha) \le n$ (since $\alpha$ satisfies $X^n - p$ over $\mathbb{Q}(\zeta)$), giving $|\mathrm{Gal}| \le \varphi(n)\cdot n$.
relatedConcepts: splitting field generated by α and ζ
prerequisites: splitting fields and roots of unity
degree of field extensions, tower law

title: Ceiling meets floor: exact order at coprime degrees
content: gal_card_eq_n_mul_totient_of_coprime (also in the imported ancestor) closes the squeeze: when gcd(n, φ(n)) = 1, the grandparent's coprime lower bound n·φ(n) ∣ |Gal| forces n·φ(n) ≤ |Gal| (Nat.le_of_dvd, |Gal| > 0), while this entry's ceiling gives |Gal| ≤ n·φ(n); Nat.le_antisymm pins |Gal| = n·φ(n) exactly. Crucially this needs no genericity hypothesis and works at every coprime degree — including n ≥ 4 where the parent's factorial squeeze (which required n·φ(n) = n!) fails. Because the two general lemmas were later merged into the ancestor InverseGaloisD4OQ02.lean (PR #31630), they are reused here through the transitive import rather than re-proved. This is what makes the quintic pin below possible.
mathContext: When $\gcd(n,\varphi(n)) = 1$, the lower divisibility $n\varphi(n) \mid |\mathrm{Gal}|$ (from $n \mid |\mathrm{Gal}|$ and $\varphi(n) \mid |\mathrm{Gal}|$ with coprimality) gives $n\varphi(n) \le |\mathrm{Gal}|$, and the ceiling gives $|\mathrm{Gal}| \le n\varphi(n)$. Antisymmetry of $\le$ on $\mathbb{N}$ forces $|\mathrm{Gal}| = n\varphi(n)$ exactly — the splitting field realizes the full holomorph.

title: Why this file proves only one of its three theorems
content: This namespace-hygiene note explains an apparent mismatch: the docstring above narrates three results (the ceiling gal_card_le_n_mul_totient, the coprime pin gal_card_eq_n_mul_totient_of_coprime, and the quintic witness gal_card_quintic_eq_twenty), yet the file below declares only the last. The two general lemmas were originally proved here but were later merged verbatim into the ancestor InverseGaloisD4OQ02.lean (PR #31630) and deleted from this file to keep a single canonical home and avoid duplicate declarations poisoning the build. They remain in scope through the transitive import (line 50), so the quintic instance can still invoke gal_card_eq_n_mul_totient_of_coprime directly. This is why meta.theoremCount is 1 even though the entry's mathematical content is the full three-theorem story: the counts track this file's own declarations, while the assumptions field documents the merge and confirms all three results remain 0-axiom in the ancestor.
mathContext: The file's contribution reduces to a single instantiation $n = 5$ of an imported general theorem; the ceiling $|\mathrm{Gal}| \le n\varphi(n)$ and coprime pin $|\mathrm{Gal}| = n\varphi(n)$ live upstream in $\texttt{InverseGaloisD4OQ02}$, imported transitively.

title: |Gal(X⁵−p)| = 20 = |F₂₀| for every prime p
content: The headline instance and this file's sole theorem: gal_card_quintic_eq_twenty pins |Gal(X⁵−p/ℚ)| = 20 = |AGL(1,5)| = |F₂₀|, uniformly in the prime p. Here gcd(5, φ(5)) = gcd(5,4) = 1, so the imported coprime bracket applies: 5·φ(5) = 20 ∣ |Gal| from below, |Gal| ≤ 20 from the ceiling. The symmetric-group bound alone is powerless — it only gives |Gal| ∣ 5! = 120, leaving 20, 40, 60, 120 all open — so the cyclotomic ceiling is essential. This is the first genuinely-new exact pin beyond the parent's n = 2, 3 factorial squeeze, exhibiting the Frobenius affine group F₂₀ as the quintic radical Galois group. The proof applies gal_card_eq_n_mul_totient_of_coprime at n = 5, then two `decide` calls evaluate Nat.Coprime 5 (φ 5) and 5·φ(5) = 20 by kernel reduction (no native_decide).
mathContext: At $n = 5$: $\varphi(5) = 4$, $\gcd(5,4) = 1$, and $5\cdot 4 = 20$. So $|\mathrm{Gal}(X^5-p/\mathbb{Q})| = 20 = |F_{20}|$, the Frobenius group $F_{20} = \mathbb{Z}/5 \rtimes \mathbb{Z}/4 = \mathrm{AGL}(1,5)$ of affine transformations $x \mapsto ax+b$ over $\mathbb{F}_5$. This is a solvable transitive subgroup of $S_5$; the factorial bound $|\mathrm{Gal}| \mid 120$ leaves $\{20,40,60,120\}$ open without the ceiling.
